source_review.notes: Checked Schmidt et al. and the original Reactor pattern; current Linux man-pages 6.18 epoll/epoll_wait, Java SE 17 Selector/SelectionKey, libuv 1.x and Libevent documentation; RFC 9293; and the cited network, systems, reliability and performance texts. Platform-specific readiness, edge/level, fairness and thread-safety statements are scoped and dated.

evidence: Checked interest/ready sets, handler budgets, service time, arrival rate, utilization, loop lag, buffer backlog and generation notation.
Confirmed utilization and cooperative round-delay expressions use consistent time/work scopes and name their assumptions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Readiness, progress, frame, handler and business completion remain explicitly separate.

evidence: Recomputed Exercise 2 budgets as 3.0 ms plus 0.2 ms overhead = 3.2 ms approximate one-round bound.
Recomputed utilization as 8,000/s times 90 microseconds = 0.72.
Reproduced two fair rounds: a/b handle 2/2 then 2/1, seven total units, both queues empty and two registrations retained.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No real syscall, kernel scheduler, network, loop-lag, callback-tail, executor, buffer or connection workload was measured.

evidence: Verified rho=lambda*E[S]<1 is necessary under the declared single-server idealization but insufficient for tail latency.
Derived the finite-ready-round delay as sum of enforced budgets plus fixed poll/dispatch overhead under fair nonblocking scheduling.
Confirmed registration/generation equality rejects stale guarded completions after close/reuse.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The arguments exclude bursts, higher-priority arrivals, shared state, unguarded external effects, kernel/runtime scheduling and distributed liveness.

evidence: Reviewed partial/zero/EOF/error/would-block operations, stale/spurious readiness, level persistence, edge under-drain, one-shot rearm and always-writable spin.
Reviewed hot/slow clients, unbounded accept/read/parse/write, timers, nested callbacks, exceptions, executor rejection, close/cancel versus completion, descriptor reuse and multi-loop skew.
Reviewed oversized/compressed/malformed frames, Slowloris, auth churn, tenant exhaustion, audit/log blocking, clinical telemetry and industrial emergency degradation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real OS/runtime/library versions, socket/TLS stacks, workloads, security controls, hardware and safety procedures require integration evidence and named human review.

evidence: Traced single owner/generation, nonblocking results, budgets/fairness, edge/level interests, watermarks, bounded offload, incremental state, idempotent close, exception containment and observability through exposition/examples/answers.
Checked finite model caps each continuously ready handler at two units, tail-requeues unfinished work and completes both without one draining its full backlog first.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits I/O, kernel notifications, clocks, threads, cancellation, pressure and lifecycle and is labeled accordingly.

evidence: Reviewed ownership argument from loop-exclusive mutable state and immutable worker snapshots/results.
Reviewed stale-completion safety from registration/generation invalidation before resource reuse and guarded application.
Reviewed fairness argument from finite ready round, tail requeue, bounded nonblocking callbacks and fair visitation.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of OS poller implementation, thread/runtime behavior, shared external state, performance, security or functional safety is claimed.

evidence: Audited ready, nonblocking, complete, fair, safe, serialized, bounded, guarantees, atomic, proof, always and conclusion language.
Confirmed product behavior, idealized model, scoped safety arguments, executable illustration, empirical testing and external review are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Readiness is consistently labeled a hint and every scheduling/lifecycle bound names its premises.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/SEPAT-071/report.json
Reproduced deterministic per-handler budgeting, tail requeue, remaining work and completion totals in Python 3.
Recorded that no real epoll/selector/libuv/libevent, socket, thread, timer, executor, pressure, cancellation, descriptor reuse, load or security test was executed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes one cooperative in-memory scheduler trace only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes Reactor readiness from Proactor completion and separates demultiplexer, registration/interest, dispatcher, handler, I/O progress, protocol state, effects and lifecycle ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers participants, partial I/O, edge/level/one-shot, interests, fairness, bounded offload, cancellation/generation, reentrancy, pressure/admission, timers, loop-per-core, security, telemetry and platform-specific testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with utilization/fairness/lifecycle models, a runnable fair-dispatch example, ten distinct boundary and production situations, and five complete exercises progressing from participant distinctions through calculation, handler design, diagnosis and industrial safety transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
